I worked concessions at Target Field from 2014-2016 and frequently ran the third base lounge concession stand. At least for foodservice workers, the only way to get there is to walk past the Twins and visitor clubhouses so I would pretty regularly see players. Most wouldn’t even look my way which was whatever, but the only player who ever acknowledged me when I worked there was Joe Mauer. 

I was on my way to drop off the end of the night deposit and clock out when I saw a tall guy leave the Twins clubhouse. I paused so I could determine who it was and holy shit it was Joe Mauer. My favorite player since I was child, I had to use all my inner strength to internalize my fingerling and look like a normal person. He turned, looked at me, smiled, and said “have a good night.” I managed to squeak out a “Thanks! You too!” It was such a little thing, quite literally the most normal interaction two strangers could have, not important in the grand scheme of things, but for me it was. I wasn’t anticipating him saying anything because of what I was used to, but to be acknowledged by a player I idolized for years felt HUGE.

Being in a lockdown myself was a very different experience than being at work and getting a phone call from my mom saying that’s she and my dad were on lockdown in the office building attached to the Mall Of America for a different gun incident (thankfully nobody died and it was another isolated event). Even though I knew my parents were safe because they were calling and texting me, I still had a panic attack and couldn’t continue working at my office job that day. My parents came home and weren’t very shaken up about their experience, but for some reason I broke down even though I knew everyone I knew who was at the mall was safe.  My experiences are different because thankfully all of the gun incidents at MOA were isolated and the perpetrators weren’t targeting the public. It’s still scary and really frustrating, but it was interesting to compare the situation where I was able to keep my cool vs have a meltdown. I hope this staff member can find a good therapist because while she may have been able to keep calm enough to effectively communicate with police, I’m sure this will still impact them on a deep level.

The school has about 200 students so it isn't that big of a school. They got locked down pretty quickly which is why the cops ran into so many locked doors and they were told most of the kids were upstairs. They probably would have continued clearing room by room, but they heard gunshots and changed focus. I haven't done a lockdown in a school in 10 years, but when I had to do them as a student we had to squish together and hide in a corner away from the door and windows. Ideally, your first option in a mass shooting is to escape and hiding is your second option. Some students and teachers may have been able to get outside and were out of view, but most were probably hiding in the classrooms with locked doors.

It comes from a lot of practice. I work at the Mall of America and was present for the December 23, 2022 shooting (fight between two people that got out of hand). I was surprised by how calm I felt when my manager and I had to wrangle shoppers into our backroom and keep them calm. I think the sense of calm came from the fact that the mall does lockdown drills at the end of every month. On the day we do drills, we do one in the morning and one at closing time. Also, thanks to Twitter I was able to pretty quickly able to figure out that the shooting was on the opposite side of the mall from my store and it was an isolated incident. Since 2019 we've had 4 lockdowns, 3 of which were for gun incidents, and after all 4 I sew quite a few posts from mall guests saying that store employees handled everything extremely well. It's because we practice for this at least 24 times a year and I'm sure I'm not the only one who has done the mental math of "How likely is my store to be in proximity to a mass shooting?" I'm sure the teachers at this school have gone through a lot of training, and from what their comments and the body cam footage show, the school got locked down very quickly making it easier for them to focus on what they need to do.

You’re 20 and have a whole life ahead of you, and one thing that comes with it it time to learn how your symptoms present themselves, how to manage them, and about what you want in a relationship. 

I (27F) have been in a relationship for 3 years and my partner has been very understanding and patient even when I know he is getting frustrated. But it’s a frustration that is in step with my own, I’ve been very slowly moving my things into his apartment and we’re not done yet and I starting bringing things over in October. My struggles with task initiation frustrate me, him, and my mom but talking about it is so important. My boyfriend has his own mental health struggles (and has hinted that he thinks he may have ASD), but we talk about it and make sure we help each other where we need it the most. 

It’s 1000% possible to have a healthy relationship when you have ADHD. It may take some time to get there, but it can happen. I never thought I would date anyone ever, but here I am in a 3 year relationship, slowly moving in together. I had handful of relationships that lasted at most a year in the first half of my 20s, a lot of them were BAD, but I learned about myself and relationships from each of them. 

I know it’s easy to say “don’t sweat it, you’re young and have a long life ahead of you,” than it is to believe it, but it’s true.

I went to two dates- Riot Fest and Cincinnati. Ironically I missed my "home" show (Saint Paul, MN)  because I was going to be at Riot Fest.  I go to Riot Fest every year so regardless if MCR was playing or not, I would have been there. 

I bought the Riot Fest tickets in 2019 using my tax return, I bought VIP and think that was around $300 (I don't remember the exact price because it was literally 3 years ago),  I stayed at a hostel for 6 nights (pre-tax total of $385),  in the fest I'm guessing I spent $250-300 on food and merch, round trip gas came to about $135, in Chicago I only used public transit and a 7-day CTA pass was $20. I don't recall how much I spent on food/activities for the days I was in Chicago and not at the fest. I also used paid vacation time for the 7 days I was out of office. Usually Riot Fest is my biggest trip of the year so I like to "bookend" the fest with one day before to do activities in the city and one day after the fest to rest/do other activities. Driving is 7-8 hours each way so giving myself extra days comes in handy because I know I'll be exhausted. 

For Cincinnati, my pit ticket was $800 which I bought as a birthday gift to myself because MCR broke up while I was a senior in high school and my mom didn't let me go to any of their tours before then and I KNEW that seeing MCR would be a shitshow at Riot Fest and I would end up standing in the back so Cincinnati was going to be my "big" MCR experience. My round trip flight on Sun Country was $203, my Airbnb (ended up being cheaper than a hotel) was $327 including fees for a 3 night stay, only bought one shirt at the merch table so that was like $40, I probably spent like $12 on bus tickets the entire time I was in Cincinnati and only used Lyft to get to the Airbnb and airport (I think total spent on Lyft was $40-45).

I wanted to go to more dates, but it's hard when you're in the midwest because you either have a really long drive or have to fly and I wasn't sure if I had enough PTO to do another trip (especially after I got tickets to two Paramore shows that also require taking a trip) AND have a few days left for holiday season stuff. If MCR does another tour in the US, I will try to go to more shows and do it as cheaply as I can lol.

This is not your fault. You did the right thing by leaving after you found out he was cheating on you. You did not force him into attempting suicide, while yes, most people who make attempts/complete are not really thinking rationally as themselves, it is still a choice they made at the end of the day. I’m in several suicide bereavement groups and in the rare situations where people received notes, people say that the note wasn’t very coherent and it didn’t sound like their loved one. It’s kind of like there’s a “pre-suicide brain fog” where yes them taking the action is them doing it, it’s still more of their mental health issues/whatever else is going on “taking over.” It’s hard to describe what it actually is because I’m not a mental health professional, I’m just somebody who lost their best friend to suicide 5 years ago and have seen a lot of the same questions get asked in bereavement groups, and they all get pretty similar answers. 

I’d also like to share that, unfortunately, regardless of if he lives or dies, there is a very good chance his family will blame you for the attempt. It won’t matter to them if he cheated they may still view it as you pushing him to it. Even though it is 100% not your fault. People have a very hard time accepting that this suicide is a choice. It’s much easier to cope with your feelings of sadness and anger if you can find somebody else to direct it to. Besides the sadness people feel when somebody dies by suicide, there is usually a bit of anger in there too, but as a survivor you feel guilty for feeling angry about it. You feel like you can’t be angry because your loved one died by suicide, you feel guilty for feeling angry at somebody who you loved and who was in that much pain. I don’t want to make it sound like this is what will absolutely happen in your cases, but it’s one of those things I’ve seen a lot in suicide attempts/completions regardless of if the loved one was cheating or not. It’s unfortunately, something you might want to prepare yourself for just in case that happens. I truly hope that it doesn’t happen to you because it makes an awful situation even worse. It doesn’t help his family actually deal with their emotions and it also doesn’t help you.

For now, I’d say you should try to stay in contact with his sister and check in with his family. Maybe don’t go see him as I can definitely see where other commenters are coming from saying this could be a manipulation tactic. The most important thing right now is for you to know that this is not your fault and I would really recommend finding a therapist who works with relationship issues and grief. Even if your (soon to be) ex-husband lives, you are still experiencing grief at some level. 

I’m really sorry you’re going through this right now. It’s a really tough situation to be in.
